newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain willing to extradite Mexican ex-prosecutor.
newsitem.headline: Spain willing to extradite Mexican ex-prosecutor.

text.p: Spain is willing to extradite the former Mexican chief prosecutor who jailed the brother of ex-president Carlos Salinas on murder charges, Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said on Wednesday.

Pablo Chapa Bezanilla was arrested on an international warrant outside a Madrid restaurant last Friday on Mexican charges of criminal association, evidence-planting and bodysnatching. He had been on the run since February.

"We are going to continue applying the mechanisms of co-operation and extradition that we have at our disposal when they are solicited," Matutes told journalists while attending a conference in north-west Spain.
"The arrest is another demonstration of the good state of relations between Spain and Mexico and of our mutual desire to extend collaboration in all areas, particularly police and judicial."

Spain and Mexico had smoothed over past troubles on judicial co-operation last year with an agreement to change their extradition treaty to allow Mexico to extradite members of Basque separatist rebel group ETA to Spain.
"The accord is working to the full satisfaction of all parties," Matutes said.
Chapa is being held in Madrid's Carabanchel prison pending the extradition request. Sources at the Mexican attorney general's office, say it should arrive in Madrid shortly.
Chapa appeared before Spain's special extradition judge on Saturday, and according to Spanish media reports, denied all charges against him and refused to return to Mexico voluntarily.

He fled Mexico after being charged with evidence-rigging and bodysnatching while acting as special prosecutor investigating the 1994 murder of Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, an official of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party.
Chapa blamed Raul Salinas, brother of former Mexican president Carlos Salinas, for the murder and had him arrested in February 1995.

But the supposed evidence linking Raul Salinas to the murder -- a skeleton found on his ranch on the outskirts of Mexico City -- then turned out to be the remains of a relative of a psychic who helped Chapa and not, as he had led the public to believe, the body of Ruiz Massieu.
Mexican authorities allege that Chapa had paid the psychic, known as "La Paca", to have a relative dug up from a cemetery and planted on Salinas' ranch.
